newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up 1.67 pct on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up 1.67 pct on foreign buying.

text.p: Late foreign buying of large capitalised stocks pushed up the Thai stocks index by 1.67 percent at the close in thin turnover on Monday, brokers said.
"Foreign investors bought several large capitalised banking issues before the market closed, pushing the SET index to rise," said a broker at a foreign brokerage house.
Brokers said turnover remained thin because investors were awaiting a U.S. Federal Reserve meeting scheduled for Tuesday.
The SET composite index closed 11.75 points higher at 713.85 on 1.9 billion baht turnover.
The SET-50 index rose 1.31 points to 53.28.
Decliners edged advancers 151 to 147 while 97 issues remained unchanged.

Brokers said a government announcement earlier in the day that the Thai current account deficit was to narrow sharply to 6.9 percent of gross domestic product this year from 8.2 percent in 1996 failed to lift market sentiment.
Investor concerns still focused on any possible hike in U.S. interest rates ahead of the Federal Reserve's Tuesday meeting.
Net foreign investor buying last Friday amounted to 245 million baht.

Most of the key sectors gained on Monday. The energy sector rose most, gaining 3.59 percent, followed by the banking sector rising 2.39 percent, and the building and furnishing materials sector advanced 2.28 percent.

Large capitalised Bangkok Bank topped the active list, rising six baht to 184. Dhana Siam Finance slipped one to 35.50, television operator BEC World dipped two to 238 and Siam Cement gained 20 to 644.
